query: Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state and a target density below 6 g/cm3, what single intervention could overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation while improving room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts measurable changes relative to the as-processed baseline, defines the relevant composition, temperature, exposure-time, and test-environment boundaries, cites supporting evidence from previously reported Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, and proposes a controlled experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

revised_generation.hypothesis: Intervention of thermal treatment can improve the performance of Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys by overcoming limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation, enhancing room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation.
revised_generation.mechanism: relaxation of metastable state and formation of stable phases
revised_generation.predicted_outcome: improved compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance
revised_generation.boundary: composition, temperature, exposure time, and test environment
revised_generation.uncertainty: effect of thermal treatment on alloy properties, and lack of specific evidence from previously reported Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys
revised_generation.falsification_experiment: controlled experiment with varying thermal treatment conditions to test the effect on alloy properties, including measurements of compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance
